candidates: When declaring a `useRef` that may hold `undefined` at runtime, type it as `useRef<T | undefined>(undefined)` rather than `useRef<T>(undefined)`; the latter is invalid under the project's strict TypeScript mode because `undefined` is not assignable to `T`.

In an if/else block that handles mutually exclusive conditions on a ref (e.g., same-story path vs. story-switch path), place each ref mutation inside the branch where it logically applies rather than hoisting it to shared scope before the branch; this makes data flow explicit and prevents unintended mutations on the wrong code path.

When resetting a tracking ref during a context switch, initialize the ref to the value from the triggering event rather than a zero/default sentinel; using a sentinel (e.g., `0`) will incorrectly satisfy any downstream guard that compares the ref's value against the event's value, causing the guard to bail out when it should not.
